questions.explanation: The graph consists of horizontal pieces at heights \(-1\) and \(1\) only, so \(f\) takes exactly the two values \(-1\) and \(1\).

questions.prompt: On the interval \(-1 < x \le 2\) the graph of a piecewise defined function is the line segment from the point \((-1, 2)\) (open circle) to the point \((2, -1)\) (solid dot). The formula for this piece is

questions.prompt: According to the Vertical Line Test, a curve in the coordinate plane is the graph of a function if and only if
options: every vertical line intersects the curve at least once
no horizontal line intersects the curve more than once
no vertical line intersects the curve more than once
the curve intersects the \(x\)-axis exactly once
questions.explanation: If a vertical line \(x = a\) met the curve twice, at \((a, b)\) and \((a, c)\), the curve would assign two different values to \(a\), which a function cannot do.

questions.prompt: Which equation does NOT define \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: \(x = y^2\) gives \(y = \pm\sqrt{x}\): for \(x = 4\) both \(y = 2\) and \(y = -2\) work. The others solve uniquely: \(y = \frac{21 - 3x}{7}\), \(y = 9 - x^2\), \(y = \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}\).

questions.prompt: Which equation defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: \(2|x| + y = 0\) gives the single value \(y = -2|x|\) for each \(x\). In \(2x + |y| = 0\), \(x = -1\) gives \(y = \pm 2\); the circle and \(x = y^4\) (\(x = 16\) gives \(y = \pm 2\)) also fail the Vertical Line Test.

questions.prompt: Consider the equations (a) \(x + y^2 = 9\) and (b) \(x^2 + y = 9\). Which of them defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: (b) gives \(y = 9 - x^2\), one value of \(y\) for each \(x\). (a) gives \(y = \pm\sqrt{9 - x}\); for \(x = 5\) both \(y = 2\) and \(y = -2\) satisfy it.

questions.prompt: Consider the equations (a) \(x = y^3\) and (b) \(x = y^4\). Which of them defines \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: (a) gives \(y = \sqrt[3]{x}\), and every real number has exactly one real cube root. (b) fails: \(x = 1\) gives both \(y = 1\) and \(y = -1\).

questions.explanation: The graph of \(f\) is the set of points \((x, f(x))\); the height of the graph above \(x = 3\) is \(f(3)\).

questions.explanation: Since \(2 \ge 2\), \(f(2) = 1\): the graph has a solid dot at \((2, 1)\) and an open circle at \((2, 0)\).

questions.explanation: Its graph is a circle, which fails the Vertical Line Test: for \(x = 0\) both \(y = 3\) and \(y = -1\) satisfy the equation.

questions.prompt: According to Definition 2.3.1, a function \(f\) is increasing on an interval \(I\) if
questions.explanation: Increasing means the graph rises from left to right: a larger input gives a larger output, \(f(x_1) < f(x_2)\) whenever \(x_1 < x_2\).

questions.prompt: Moving from left to right, the graph of \(f\) rises from the point \(A\) at \(x=a\) to \(B\) at \(x=b\), falls from \(B\) to \(C\) at \(x=c\), and rises again from \(C\) to \(D\) at \(x=d\). On which interval is \(f\) decreasing?
questions.explanation: The graph falls between \(B\) and \(C\), so \(f\) is decreasing on \([b, c]\); it is increasing on \([a,b]\) and on \([c,d]\).

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x) = x^{2/3}\). On which intervals is \(f\) decreasing and increasing?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y = x^{2/3}\) falls to the point \((0,0)\) and then rises, so \(f\) is decreasing on \((-\infty, 0]\) and increasing on \([0, \infty)\) (Example 2.10).

questions.prompt: Starting from \(y = \sqrt{x}\), the graph of \(y = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x+4} - 3\) has its endpoint (starting point) at
questions.explanation: Shift left 4, shrink vertically by \(\frac{1}{2}\), then shift down 3: the endpoint \((0,0)\) of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) moves to \((-4, -3)\) (Problem 5).

questions.explanation: Reflecting gives \(y = -x^2\); shifting up 1 adds 1: \(y = 1 - x^2\), a parabola with vertex \((0,1)\) opening downward (Problem 9).

questions.prompt: The vertex of the parabola \(f(x) = (x+7)^2\) is
questions.explanation: Replacing \(x\) by \(x + 7\) shifts \(y = x^2\) left 7 units, so the vertex moves from \((0,0)\) to \((-7, 0)\) (Problem 10).

questions.prompt: For \(y = 2 - \sqrt{x+1}\), the domain and the starting point of the graph are
questions.explanation: Shift \(y=\sqrt{x}\) left 1, reflect in the \(x\)-axis, shift up 2. We need \(x + 1 \ge 0\), so the domain is \(x \ge -1\), and at \(x=-1\) we get \(y = 2\) (Problem 12).

questions.prompt: The parabola \(y = 3 - 2(x-1)^2\) has vertex
questions.explanation: Shift \(y=x^2\) right 1, multiply by \(-2\) (reflect and stretch by 2), then shift up 3: the vertex is \((1, 3)\) and the parabola opens downward (Problem 13).

questions.prompt: The graph of \(y = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 1\) is obtained from the graph of \(y = x^3\) by

questions.prompt: Which equation gives the graph of \(y = |x|\) shifted 1 unit to the right?
questions.explanation: A shift to the right by 1 replaces \(x\) by \(x - 1\): \(y = |x - 1|\), with vertex \((1, 0)\). \(y = |x| - 1\) is a shift down (Problems 7 and 15).

questions.prompt: The graph of \(y = |x|\) is reflected in the \(x\)-axis and then shifted upward 2 units. The resulting equation is
questions.explanation: Reflecting gives \(y = -|x|\); adding 2 shifts it up: \(y = 2 - |x|\), an inverted V with vertex \((0, 2)\) (Problem 16).

questions.explanation: \(y = f(x - c)\) is shifted to the right \(c\) units; \(y = f(x + c)\) is the one shifted to the left.

questions.explanation: \(f(-x) = (-x)^2 + (-x) = x^2 - x\), which is neither \(f(x)\) nor \(-f(x)\); \(f\) is neither even nor odd (Problem 18).

questions.explanation: For an odd function \(f(-x) = -f(x)\): rotating the graph \(180^\circ\) about the origin gives the same graph, as for \(f(x) = x^3\).

questions.prompt: The graph of \(f(x) = -x^3\) is obtained from the graph of \(y = x^3\) by reflecting it in the \(x\)-axis.
questions.explanation: Multiplying \(y = x^3\) by \(-1\) gives \(y = -f(x)\), the reflection in the \(x\)-axis (Problem 11).

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x) = x^{-3} = \frac{1}{x^3}\) is an odd function.
questions.explanation: \(f(-x) = \frac{1}{(-x)^3} = \frac{1}{-x^3} = -\frac{1}{x^3} = -f(x)\), so \(f\) is odd and its graph is symmetric about the origin (Problem 22).

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=x^2-9\) and \(g(x)=\sqrt{x+1}\). Then \(f\circ g\) is

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=2x+1\), \(g(x)=x^2\) and \(h(x)=x-3\). Then \((f\circ g\circ h)(x)=\)

questions.prompt: According to the definition, a function \(f\) is one-to-one (injective) if
options: every horizontal line meets its graph at least once
no vertical line meets its graph more than once
questions.explanation: One-to-one means \(f\) never takes the same value twice: \(f(x_1)=f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1=x_2\) (equivalently \(x_1\ne x_2 \Rightarrow f(x_1)\ne f(x_2)\)). Option B holds for every function, and D is the vertical line test for being a function.

questions.prompt: The horizontal line \(y=4\) meets the graph of a function \(f\) at the two points \((-2,4)\) and \((2,4)\). What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: Horizontal line test: a function is one-to-one if and only if no horizontal line meets its graph more than once. Here \(f(-2)=f(2)=4\) with \(-2\ne 2\), so \(f\) is not one-to-one (and has no inverse function).

questions.prompt: Let \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and let \(g\) be the function on \(A\) given by \(g(1)=5,\ g(2)=4,\ g(3)=4\). Which statement is true?
options: \(g\) is one-to-one because every element of \(A\) has an image
questions.explanation: \(g\) takes the value 4 twice (\(g(2)=g(3)=4\) with \(2\ne 3\)), so it is not one-to-one, exactly like the arrow diagram in Figure 2.13. Every element having an image only makes \(g\) a function.

questions.prompt: To show that \(f(x)=3x+4\) is onto (surjective), we take any real number \(y\) and solve \(y=3x+4\) for \(x\). The result is
questions.explanation: Subtract 4 then divide by 3: \(3x=y-4\), so \(x=\frac{y-4}{3}\in\mathbb{R}\). Every \(y\) in the codomain is an image, so \(f\) is onto; being also one-to-one, \(f\) is bijective.

questions.prompt: A one-to-one function \(f\) has domain \([2,\infty)\) and range \([0,\infty)\). Then its inverse \(f^{-1}\) has
questions.explanation: By the definition of the inverse, domain of \(f^{-1}\) = range of \(f\) = \([0,\infty)\) and range of \(f^{-1}\) = domain of \(f\) = \([2,\infty)\). The endpoints stay closed.

questions.prompt: If \(f(1)=5\), \(f(3)=7\) and \(f(8)=-10\) for a one-to-one function \(f\), then \(f^{-1}(7)=\)
To find the inverse of a one-to-one function \(f\), we write \(y=f(x)\), solve this equation for \(x\) in terms of \(y\), and then
options: take the reciprocal of both sides

questions.explanation: Steps: (1) write \(y=f(x)\); (2) solve for \(x\) in terms of \(y\); (3) interchange \(x\) and \(y\) to get \(y=f^{-1}(x)\). Steps 2 and 3 may also be done in the other order.

questions.prompt: Find the inverse of the function \(f(x)=3x-2\).
questions.explanation: From \(y=3x-2\): \(3x=y+2\), so \(x=\frac{y+2}{3}\). Interchanging \(x\) and \(y\) gives \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+2}{3}\).

questions.prompt: Find the inverse of the function \(f(x)=\frac{x^5-3}{2}\).
The point \((3,-5)\) lies on the graph of a one-to-one function \(f\). Which point must lie on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.explanation: If \(f(a)=b\) then \(f^{-1}(b)=a\), so \((a,b)\) on the graph of \(f\) gives \((b,a)\) on the graph of \(f^{-1}\): here \((3,-5)\) becomes \((-5,3)\). This is the reflection in the line \(y=x\).

questions.prompt: Find an equation for the inverse of \(f(x)=\sqrt{x-2}\).
questions.explanation: Swap \(x\) and \(y\) in \(y=\sqrt{x-2}\): \(x=\sqrt{y-2}\). Square: \(x^2=y-2\), so \(y=x^2+2\). Thus \(f^{-1}(x)=x^2+2\) with domain \([0,\infty)\).

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\sqrt{x-2}\). The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is
questions.explanation: The domain of \(f^{-1}\) equals the range of \(f\). Since \(\sqrt{x-2}\ge 0\), the range of \(f\) is \([0,\infty)\), so \(f^{-1}(x)=x^2+2\) is defined only for \(x\ge 0\). \([2,\infty)\) is the domain of \(f\), i.e. the range of \(f^{-1}\).

questions.prompt: Which of the following functions is NOT one-to-one?

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\frac{3-x}{4}\). Which function \(g\) satisfies \(f(g(x))=x\) and \(g(f(x))=x\) for every real \(x\)?
questions.explanation: \(f(g(x))=\frac{3-(3-4x)}{4}=\frac{4x}{4}=x\) and \(g(f(x))=3-(3-x)=x\). By the Inverse Function Property, \(f\) and \(g\) are inverses. With \(4x-3\) one gets \(f(4x-3)=\frac{6-4x}{4}\ne x\).

questions.prompt: Find the inverse of \(f(x)=\frac{1+3x}{5-2x}\).
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply \(y(5-2x)=1+3x\): \(5y-1=3x+2xy=x(2y+3)\), so \(x=\frac{5y-1}{2y+3}\). Interchange: \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{5x-1}{2x+3}\). The reciprocal \(\frac{5-2x}{1+3x}\) is not the inverse.

questions.prompt: Find the inverse of \(f(x)=\frac{4x-7}{3x+1}\).

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\frac{4x-7}{3x+1}\). Which value is NOT in the domain of \(f^{-1}\)?

questions.explanation: Solve \(x^2-4x+(5-y)=0\): \(x=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{4y-4}}{2}\), i.e. \(x=2\pm\sqrt{y-1}\). The domain \(x\ge 2\) selects the \(+\) sign, so \(f^{-1}(x)=2+\sqrt{x-1}\), \(x\ge 1\).

Let \(f(x)=9-x^2\), \(x\ge 0\). The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is
questions.explanation: Domain of \(f^{-1}\) = range of \(f\). For \(x\ge 0\), \(9-x^2\) starts at 9 and decreases without bound, so the range is \((-\infty,9]\); indeed \(f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{9-x}\) needs \(x\le 9\).

questions.prompt: If some horizontal line intersects the graph of a function \(f\) at two different points, then \(f\) is not one-to-one.
questions.explanation: Two points \((x_1,c)\) and \((x_2,c)\) on the graph mean \(f(x_1)=f(x_2)\) with \(x_1\ne x_2\), so \(f\) is not one-to-one (horizontal line test).

questions.prompt: The functions \(f(x)=x^3\) and \(g(x)=\frac{1}{x^3}\) are inverses of each other.
questions.explanation: \(g(f(x))=\frac{1}{x^9}\ne x\). The inverse of \(x^3\) is the cube root \(x^{1/3}\); the symbol \(f^{-1}\) does not mean \(\frac{1}{f}\).

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x)=6-x\) is its own inverse, that is \(f^{-1}(x)=6-x\).
questions.explanation: From \(y=6-x\) we get \(x=6-y\); interchanging gives \(f^{-1}(x)=6-x=f(x)\). Check: \(f(f(x))=6-(6-x)=x\).

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x)=x^2+2\) is one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\).
questions.explanation: \(f(1)=f(-1)=3\) with \(1\ne-1\), so \(f\) takes the same value twice; the horizontal line \(y=3\) meets the parabola at two points.

questions.prompt: If \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+3}\), \(x\ge-3\), then \(f^{-1}(x)=x^2-3\) with domain \([0,\infty)\).
questions.explanation: Swap and square: \(x=\sqrt{y+3}\Rightarrow y=x^2-3\). The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), which is \([0,\infty)\).
